title: Do high-market-cap tokens have MORE shared-funding creators than the rest?
whyReversed:
v0.2 predicted that non-graduated tokens would cluster MORE, on the theory that manufactured backing predicts failure. It returned a null: 27.9% against 24.2%, p=0.203. The null stands and is not withdrawn.

The reason it was uninformative is that its outcome was wrong. `complete` means a bonding curve filled, not that a token succeeded: the median graduated token in that window had a market cap of $1,539. Both arms were overwhelmingly failures, so the comparison was failures-that-graduated against failures-that-did-not.

An exploratory re-analysis using market cap, at thresholds chosen AFTER seeing the distribution, found the opposite of the v0.2 prediction: above $10M, 50% of winning creators sat in a shared-funding cluster against 21% of the rest, p=0.010 raw and 0.040 after Bonferroni for four thresholds. That is a lead, not a result -- n=16, and moving two tokens across the line takes p from 0.010 to 0.123.

This registration tests that lead properly, and predicts the REVERSED direction in advance so it cannot be claimed either way after the fact.
hypothesis: Shared funding infrastructure is a competence signal, not a fraud signal: operators with real distribution launch repeatedly from shared funding, amateurs launch once from a fresh wallet.

population.freshWindowRule: the window MUST NOT overlap v0.2's, which ran 2026-08-10 15:13 to 2026-08-11 17:35 UTC. Any token whose created_timestamp falls inside that range is discarded. The lead was generated on that data and cannot be confirmed by it.
population.frame: all tokens retrievable in the fresh window, graduated or not

outcome.whyFixedNow: $10M is fixed here, before the fresh population exists, because it is the threshold the lead appeared at. Re-tuning it after collection would be choosing the bar that makes the result work -- and the v0.2 experiment exists precisely because that error is easy.
outcome.noOtherThresholdMayBeReported: exactly one threshold is tested. v0.2's exploratory pass tried four and one reached significance; testing several again would reintroduce the multiple-comparison problem the Bonferroni correction only partly answered.

exposure.measure: creator sits in a multi-creator shared-funding cluster
exposure.whyOneHop: v0.2 specified three hops and implemented one. Rather than silently keep the mismatch, one hop is registered as the measure. Deeper ancestry is a separate question and would be a separate registration.
exposure.hubRule: a funder of 25 or more creators, or one whose history could not be fully retrieved, is a HUB and merges nothing. Failing closed pushes the measured effect toward null, which is the safe direction for a hypothesis we now expect to be true.

endpoint.H0: winners and the rest have the same shared-funding clustering rate
endpoint.failCondition: p >= 0.05, or winners cluster LESS. A result in the v0.2 direction is a failure of THIS registration, not a revival of that one.

effectRequires.property: at least 30 winners above the threshold in the fresh window
effectRequires.why: the lead rests on n=16, where two tokens move p across 0.05. Below 30 the run cannot improve on what generated it, and STOPS rather than reporting a second fragile number.

effectRequires.property: at least one multi-creator cluster exists

stopRule: collect until the winner count reaches 30 or the API's reachable window is exhausted, whichever comes first. The threshold is never lowered to reach 30.
